nodes.procedure: The as-prepared precursor was put in a tube furnace under nitrogen for phosphorating process at 350°C, leading to the construction of Ni₂P/CoP nanosheets, as reported in the previous work.

nodes.name: Pt Electrodeposition on TMP (10s)
nodes.procedure: Pt nanocrystals were grown on the edge of Ni₂P/CoP nanosheets by an electrodeposition method in a three-electrode cell with platinum foil and Ag/AgCl as counter and reference electrodes, respectively, for 10 s. The detailed synthesis was described in the supporting information.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows uniform vertical Ni₂P/CoP nanosheets with high curvature and small Pt nanocrystals grown on the edges after 10 s electrodeposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The uniform Ni₂P/CoP nanosheets were shown in Figure 2a by scanning electron microscope (SEM). ... There were small Pt nanocrystals on the edge of nanosheets after 10 s electrodeposition, illustrated in Figure 2b

properties.annotation: blue box and arrow highlighting specific region

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows Ni₂P/CoP nanosheets surrounded by Pt nanocrystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2c shows that Ni₂P/CoP nanosheets were surrounded by Pt nanocrystals.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacing of 2.26 Å corresponding to the (111) plane of Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image shows the lattice space of 2.26Å, corresponding to the (111) plane of Pt in Figure 2d.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms successful fabrication of Ni₂P/CoP nanosheets on Ni foams but shows no obvious diffraction peaks from crystallized Pt metals due to ultralow Pt loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Figure S4, Supporting Information) illustrate the successful fabrication of Ni₂P/CoP nanosheets on Ni foams. However, with ultra-low loading of Pt species, XRD patterns of the catalysts showed no obvious diffraction peaks from crystalized Pt metals or metal oxides.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p peaks at 857.1 eV and 874.9 eV, Co 2p peaks at 778.9/782.2 eV and 794.1/798.1 eV, P 2p peaks at 130.0, 131.3, and 134.6 eV, and Pt 4f metallic Pt⁰ peaks at 71.3 eV and 74.4 eV confirming formation of Pt nanocrystals on Ni₂P/CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the deconvolution, two peaks located at 857.1 eV and 874.9 eV correspond to Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂ in Figure 3a. ... Figure 3d presents the XPS spectrum of Pt 4f. The paired peaks located at 71.3 eV and 74.4 eV correspond to metallic Pt⁰, indicating the formation of Pt nanocrystals.

nodes.characterization_summary: MP-AES shows Pt mass percentage of 0.38 wt% in Ni₂P/CoP-Pt 10s sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt mass percentages in Ni₂P/CoP-Pt samples with the electrodeposition time of 10, 50, and 100s were examined by microwave plasma atomic emission spectrometers (MP-AES), which were 0.38, 0.71, and 0.96 wt%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV with scan rates from 50 to 100 mV s⁻¹ gives double-layer capacitance (Cdl) of 68.1 mF cm⁻² for Ni₂P/CoP-Pt 10s, indicating increased active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical active surface area (ECSA) was studied by cyclic voltammetry (CV) with scan rates from 50 to 100 mV s⁻¹ (Figure S8, Supporting Information). The double-layer capacitance (Cdl) of Ni foam-Pt 10s, Ni₂P/CoP, and Ni₂P/CoP-Pt 10s are 0.53, 46.7, and 68.1 mF cm⁻², respectively (Figure S9, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows smaller charge transfer resistance (Rct) for Ni₂P/CoP-Pt 10s compared to Ni₂P/CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni₂P/CoP-Pt 10s shows smaller Rct compared with Ni₂P/CoP, indicating faster charge transfer with extra Pt loading.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAABF-STEM after 80 h durability test shows Pt nanocrystals remain on the edge of nanosheets with no obvious size change.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular bright-field-scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAABF-STEM) image (Figure S10b, Supporting Information) showed that Pt nanocrystals were on the edge of nanosheets, with no obvious change of sizes.
